question: What is the frequency (f) of a wave with a period of 0.04 seconds?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 25 Hz.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Frequency (f) and time period (T) of a wave are reciprocals of each other:

◦ f = 1 / T

◦ Here T = 0.04 s, so f = 1 / 0.04 = 25 Hz. (आवृत्ति = 1 / आवर्तकाल)

• Frequency is the number of complete waves (oscillations) produced per second; its SI unit is the hertz (Hz), named after the physicist Heinrich Hertz.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Time period (T) is the time taken to complete one full oscillation; its SI unit is the second.

• Other wave relations: v = f λ (wave speed = frequency × wavelength). Amplitude is the maximum displacement from the mean position and determines loudness in sound.

NOTE

• Audible range of the human ear: 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz. Below 20 Hz is infrasound and above 20,000 Hz is ultrasound (used in sonography, SONAR and cleaning). Speed of sound in air is about 343 m/s at 20 °C.

question: International Day of Non-violence is observed on ___________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2 October.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The International Day of Non-violence is observed every year on 2 October, the birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi (Gandhi Jayanti), who pioneered the philosophy and strategy of non-violence (ahimsa). (अंतर्राष्ट्रीय अहिंसा दिवस — 2 अक्टूबर)

• It was established by a resolution of the United Nations General Assembly on 15 June 2007.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Mahatma Gandhi (1869–1948) was born at Porbandar, Gujarat; he is called the Father of the Nation and Bapu.

• Gandhiji's key movements: Champaran Satyagraha (1917), Kheda Satyagraha (1918), Non-Cooperation Movement (1920), Civil Disobedience/Dandi March (1930), Quit India Movement (1942).

NOTE

• Other Indian national days: 15 August — Independence Day; 26 January — Republic Day; 26 November — Constitution Day (Samvidhan Divas); 2 October — Gandhi Jayanti and also the birth anniversary of Lal Bahadur Shastri.

question: Which of the following wars took place in the year 1761?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Panipat III.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Third Battle of Panipat was fought on 14 January 1761 between the Marathas (led by Sadashivrao Bhau, with Vishwasrao) and the Afghan invader Ahmad Shah Abdali (Durrani), supported by Najib-ud-Daula of Rohilkhand and the Nawab of Awadh. (पानीपत का तीसरा युद्ध — 1761)

• The Marathas suffered a crushing defeat, which halted their northward expansion and indirectly cleared the way for British supremacy in India.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Battle of Buxar — 1764: the British (Hector Munro) defeated the combined forces of Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daula and Shah Alam II, leading to the Treaty of Allahabad (1765) and the grant of Diwani rights of Bengal, Bihar and Odisha to the East India Company.

• Battle of Wandiwash — 1760: the English (Sir Eyre Coote) defeated the French (Count de Lally) in the Third Carnatic War, ending French ambitions in India.

• Second Battle of Panipat — 1556: Akbar/Bairam Khan defeated Hemu (Hemchandra Vikramaditya).

NOTE

• First Battle of Panipat — 1526: Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi, founding the Mughal Empire and introducing Tulughma tactics and field artillery in India. All three Panipat battles were fought in present-day Haryana.

question: The Sarda River rises in the ________ glacier in the Nepal Himalayas.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Milam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Sarda (Sharda) River, also known as the Kali or Mahakali river in its upper course, rises from the Milam Glacier in the Nepal Himalayas. (शारदा नदी — मिलम ग्लेशियर)

• It flows along the India–Nepal border and later joins the Ghaghara (Karnali), which is a left-bank tributary of the Ganga.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Bokhar Chu glacier (in the Mansarovar–Kailash region of Tibet) is the source of the Sutlej.

• Siachen Glacier (in the Karakoram range, Ladakh) is one of the largest glaciers outside the polar regions and feeds the Nubra river.

• Machoi Glacier (Jammu & Kashmir) is a source of the Dras river.

NOTE

• Sources of major Himalayan rivers: Ganga — Gangotri Glacier (Bhagirathi); Yamuna — Yamunotri Glacier; Indus — near Lake Mansarovar, Tibet; Brahmaputra — Chemayungdung Glacier (Angsi), Tibet; Alaknanda — Satopanth Glacier.

question: Which of the following iron and steel plants is located in Odisha?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rourkela.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Rourkela Steel Plant is located in the Sundargarh district of Odisha. It was the first integrated public-sector steel plant in India, set up in 1955 with German (West German) collaboration and commissioned in 1959. (राउरकेला इस्पात संयंत्र — ओडिशा)

• It is managed by the Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Vijaynagar (Vidyanagar) Steel Plant — Bellary district, Karnataka (JSW Steel).

• Bokaro Steel Plant — Jharkhand, set up with Soviet (Russian) collaboration.

• Visakhapatnam Steel Plant — Andhra Pradesh, India's first shore-based integrated steel plant (RINL).

NOTE

• Steel plants with foreign collaboration: Rourkela – Germany, Bhilai (Chhattisgarh) – USSR, Durgapur (West Bengal) – Britain (UK), Bokaro (Jharkhand) – USSR.

• Odisha is India's leading producer of iron ore, bauxite and chromite; the Sundargarh–Keonjhar–Mayurbhanj belt is rich in iron ore.

question:
What is the product of the following chemical reaction?

NaCl + H2O + CO2 + NH3
solution_text:
The correct answer is Baking soda.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The reaction of sodium chloride (NaCl) + water (H₂O) + carbon dioxide (CO₂) + ammonia (NH₃) produces sodium hydrogen carbonate (NaHCO₃), commonly called baking soda. This is the Solvay (ammonia–soda) process. (खाने का सोडा — सोडियम बाइकार्बोनेट)

◦ NaCl + H₂O + CO₂ + NH₃ → NH₄Cl + NaHCO₃

• Baking soda (NaHCO₃) is a mild, non-corrosive base; it is used in baking (as it releases CO₂ on heating, making cakes fluffy), in soda–acid fire extinguishers, and as an antacid to neutralise excess stomach acid.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Bleaching powder — Ca(OCl)Cl / CaOCl₂: made by passing chlorine over dry slaked lime, Ca(OH)₂; used for bleaching and disinfecting drinking water.

• Gypsum — CaSO₄·2H₂O: used in making Plaster of Paris and cement.

• Washing soda — Na₂CO₃·10H₂O: obtained by heating baking soda to get sodium carbonate, which is then recrystallised; used for cleaning and removing the permanent hardness of water.

NOTE

• Chain of formation: NaCl → NaHCO₃ (baking soda) → Na₂CO₃ (washing soda).

• Common names: Common salt — NaCl; Caustic soda — NaOH; Lime water — Ca(OH)₂; Quick lime — CaO; Plaster of Paris — CaSO₄·½H₂O.

question: Minor points called 'Yuko' are part of which of the following sports?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Judo.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Yuko" is a scoring term in Judo used for a minor score/point awarded for a throw or hold of lesser effectiveness than a full-point throw. (जूडो — युको)

• Judo scoring terms: Ippon (a full point that wins the contest immediately), Waza-ari (a half point), and Yuko (a minor point in the older scoring system).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Judo was founded by Jigoro Kano of Japan in 1882. It became an Olympic sport for men at the Tokyo Olympics, 1964, and for women at Barcelona, 1992.

• The judo playing area is called a tatami; the practice hall is a dojo; the uniform is a judogi. Rank is shown by the colour of the belt (obi).

• Other judo terms: Osaekomi (hold), Shido (penalty), Hajime (start), Matte (wait), Sonomama (do not move).

NOTE

• India's first Olympic medal in judo is yet to come, but Sushila Devi Likmabam has represented India at the Olympics. Tulika Maan won a silver at the Commonwealth Games 2022.

question: At which sports event in India is the Raja Bhalindra Singh Trophy awarded?
solution_text:
The correct answer is National Games of India.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Raja Bhalindra Singh Trophy is awarded at the National Games of India to the best-performing state/contingent (the overall champion team) of the Games. (राजा भालिंद्र सिंह ट्रॉफी — राष्ट्रीय खेल)

• It is named after Raja Bhalindra Singh, a former President of the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) and a member of the International Olympic Committee.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The National Games are organised by the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) along with the host state.

• The 36th National Games (2022) were held in Gujarat, the 37th (2023) in Goa and the 38th (2025) in Uttarakhand.

• Services Sports Control Board (Services) has won the Raja Bhalindra Singh Trophy many times, as have Maharashtra and Haryana.

NOTE

• Other Indian sports honours: Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award (highest sporting honour), Arjuna Award (outstanding performance), Dronacharya Award (coaches), Dhyan Chand Award (lifetime achievement), Maulana Abul Kalam Azad (MAKA) Trophy (best university in inter-university sports).

question: Which great Indian classical dancer choreographed the songs for Madhuri Dixit in 'Devdas' and 'Dil To Pagal Hai' movies?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Birju Maharaj.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pandit Birju Maharaj, the legendary Kathak maestro, choreographed songs for Madhuri Dixit in the films "Devdas" (the song *Kaahe Ched Mohe*) and "Dil To Pagal Hai". (पंडित बिरजू महाराज — कथक)

• He belonged to the Lucknow "Kalka-Bindadin" gharana of Kathak and was the son of Achhan Maharaj.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Birju Maharaj was honoured with the Padma Vibhushan (1986), the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award and a National Film Award for Best Choreography (2012) for the film *Vishwaroopam*.

• He also choreographed for films such as Shatranj Ke Khiladi, Umrao Jaan (2006) and Bajirao Mastani.

NOTE

• Kathak is the classical dance of North India (Uttar Pradesh), marked by fast footwork (tatkar), chakkars (spins) and abhinaya; its main gharanas are Lucknow, Jaipur and Banaras.

• Other options: Prabhu Deva and Farah Khan are film choreographers, and Ganesh Hegde is a dancer-choreographer, but none is a classical dance maestro of Birju Maharaj's stature.

question: Which famous medieval singer was born in Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh in the year 1506?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tansen.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mian Tansen (originally Ramtanu Pandey) was born in 1506 at Behat near Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh. He was one of the greatest musicians of medieval India and one of the Navaratnas (nine gems) in the court of Emperor Akbar. (तानसेन — ग्वालियर, 1506)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Tansen is credited with creating ragas such as Miyan ki Malhar, Miyan ki Todi and Darbari Kanada. Legend says he could light lamps by singing Raga Deepak and bring rain with Raga Megh Malhar.

• He learnt music from Swami Haridas of Vrindavan and later from Muhammad Ghaus. His tomb is at Gwalior, where the Tansen Samaroh music festival is held every year.

• Akbar's Navaratnas included Birbal, Abul Fazl, Faizi, Tansen, Raja Todar Mal, Raja Man Singh, Abdul Rahim Khan-i-Khanan, Fakir Aziao-Din and Mullah Do Piaza.

NOTE

• Gopal Nayek was a musician of the era of Alauddin Khalji; Swami Haridas was Tansen's teacher and a great devotional singer; Chaitanya Mahaprabhu was a Bhakti saint of Bengal who popularised Sankirtana.

question: If a citizen is helping the government in protecting the monuments in his/her area, which of the following fundamental duties is he/she performing?
option_3: Valuing and preserving the rich heritage and culture
solution_text:
The correct answer is Valuing and preserving the rich heritage and culture.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Helping the government protect monuments is part of the Fundamental Duty "to value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture", given in Article 51A(f) of the Constitution. (मूल कर्तव्य — सांस्कृतिक विरासत का संरक्षण)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Fundamental Duties were added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee, and are listed in Part IV-A, Article 51A.

• Originally 10 duties were added; the 11th duty — for a parent/guardian to provide education opportunities to a child between 6 and 14 years — was added by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002.

• Some duties: to abide by the Constitution and respect the National Flag and Anthem; to cherish the noble ideals of the freedom struggle; to protect the sovereignty and integrity of India; to promote harmony; to protect the natural environment; to develop scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform.

NOTE

• Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable (not enforceable by courts) and were borrowed from the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR (Russia).

question: In which year was the first-ever motion to remove a Supreme Court Justice signed by the members of Parliament?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1991.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The first-ever motion for the removal (impeachment) of a Supreme Court judge in India was signed by Members of Parliament in 1991, against Justice V. Ramaswami of the Supreme Court, on charges of financial irregularities. (न्यायमूर्ति वी. रामास्वामी — 1991)

• The motion was taken up in the Lok Sabha in 1993, but it failed because the Congress party abstained and the motion could not get the required special majority.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Removal procedure — Article 124(4): a judge of the Supreme Court can be removed by an order of the President, after an address by each House of Parliament supported by a majority of the total membership of that House and a majority of not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting, on the ground of proved misbehaviour or incapacity.

• The process is governed by the Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968. The motion needs 100 members in the Lok Sabha or 50 members in the Rajya Sabha to be admitted.

NOTE

• No judge of the Supreme Court or a High Court has ever been successfully removed in India. Justice Soumitra Sen (Calcutta HC) resigned in 2011 after the Rajya Sabha passed the motion, before the Lok Sabha could vote.

question: Which of the following communicable diseases is caused by bacteria?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cholera.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Cholera is a bacterial disease caused by Vibrio cholerae. It spreads through contaminated water and food and causes severe watery diarrhoea, vomiting and dehydration. (हैज़ा — जीवाणु जनित रोग)

• Treatment relies on Oral Rehydration Solution (ORS) and antibiotics; prevention depends on safe drinking water and sanitation.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Malaria is caused by a protozoan — Plasmodium (P. vivax, P. falciparum), transmitted by the female Anopheles mosquito.

• Dengue is caused by a virus (Dengue virus) spread by the Aedes aegypti mosquito; it causes high fever and a fall in platelet count.

• Influenza (flu) is caused by the influenza virus and spreads through air droplets.

NOTE

• Other bacterial diseases: tuberculosis (Mycobacterium tuberculosis), typhoid (Salmonella typhi), tetanus, diphtheria, plague, leprosy, whooping cough, anthrax.

• Other viral diseases: AIDS, COVID-19, polio, measles, mumps, chickenpox, rabies, hepatitis, common cold.

question: Suspended solids in water can increase the haziness of the water. Which of the following represents the measurement of haziness of water?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Turbidity.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Turbidity" is the measure of the cloudiness or haziness of a liquid caused by suspended solid particles that scatter light. High turbidity means poor water quality. (जल की गंदलापन/धुंधलापन — टर्बिडिटी)

• Turbidity is measured with a nephelometer/turbidity meter and expressed in NTU (Nephelometric Turbidity Units).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Solubility is the maximum amount of a solute that can dissolve in a given quantity of solvent at a given temperature.

• Salinity is the amount of dissolved salts in water (average ocean salinity is about 35 ppt).

• Viscosity is the resistance of a fluid to flow (honey has higher viscosity than water).

NOTE

• Drinking-water standards in India (BIS/IS 10500) recommend turbidity of 1 NTU or less (acceptable limit 1, permissible 5 NTU).

• Turbidity is reduced during water treatment by coagulation (using alum), flocculation, sedimentation and filtration, followed by chlorination for disinfection.

question: In June 2023, who was appointed as the new Research and Analysis Wing (RAW) chief?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ravi Sinha.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In June 2023, Ravi Sinha, a 1988-batch IPS officer of the Chhattisgarh cadre, was appointed the new Secretary (Research), i.e., the chief of the Research and Analysis Wing (RAW). He took charge on 30 June 2023, succeeding Samant Kumar Goel. (रवि सिन्हा — रॉ प्रमुख)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• RAW (Research and Analysis Wing) is India's external intelligence agency, established in 1968 after the 1962 and 1965 wars; its first chief was R. N. Kao.

• RAW functions under the Cabinet Secretariat and reports directly to the Prime Minister. Its motto is "Dharmo Rakshati Rakshitah" (the law protects those who protect it). Headquarters: New Delhi.

NOTE

• Intelligence Bureau (IB), founded in 1887, is India's internal intelligence agency and works under the Ministry of Home Affairs. Rajiv Kumar was the Chief Election Commissioner of India, not the RAW chief.

question: In 1917, Mahatma Gandhi started his first satyagraha in India against the forced cultivation of indigo by Europeans in which of the following districts of British India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Champaran.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Champaran Satyagraha (1917) in the Champaran district of Bihar was Mahatma Gandhi's first satyagraha in India. It was launched against the "Tinkathia" system, under which peasants were forced by European planters to grow indigo (neel) on 3/20th of their land. (चंपारण सत्याग्रह — 1917)

• Gandhiji went there at the request of the local peasant leader Raj Kumar Shukla. The agitation succeeded and the Champaran Agrarian Act, 1918 abolished the Tinkathia system.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Kheda Satyagraha (1918, Gujarat) — a no-tax campaign by peasants who could not pay revenue after crop failure; Gandhiji was assisted by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and Indulal Yagnik.

• Ahmedabad Mill Strike (1918) — Gandhiji's first hunger strike, in support of the demands of cotton mill workers.

• The Battle of Buxar (1764) is unrelated to Gandhian movements.

NOTE

• Associates of Gandhiji at Champaran: Rajendra Prasad, Brajkishore Prasad, Anugrah Narayan Sinha, J. B. Kripalani and Mahadev Desai.

• Gandhiji returned to India from South Africa in 1915; his political mentor was Gopal Krishna Gokhale.

question: After the ________ of Hakim Mirza, Kabul was annexed by Akbar and given to Raja Man Singh as ‘jagir’.
solution_text:
The correct answer is death.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mirza Muhammad Hakim was Akbar's half-brother and the ruler of Kabul. After his death in 1585, Akbar annexed Kabul to the Mughal Empire and assigned it as a jagir to Raja Man Singh of Amber. (हकीम मिर्ज़ा की मृत्यु के बाद काबुल अकबर के अधीन आया)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• A "jagir" was a land assignment given to a noble in lieu of a salary; the holder was called a jagirdar. The related administrative system was the Mansabdari system introduced by Akbar in 1571, based on Zat (personal rank/status) and Sawar (cavalry rank).

• Raja Man Singh I of Amber was one of Akbar's Navaratnas and his greatest Rajput general; he led the Mughal army at the Battle of Haldighati (1576) against Maharana Pratap.

NOTE

• Akbar (r. 1556–1605) also abolished the jizya (1564) and the pilgrimage tax, founded the Din-i-Ilahi (1582) and built Fatehpur Sikri and the Ibadat Khana. He shifted his attention to the north-west after 1585, staying at Lahore for over a decade.

question: In January 2024, Prime Minister Narendra Modi paid tributes to Savitribai Phule on her birth anniversary. In which field did Savitribai Phule make significant contributions, as highlighted by Prime Minister Modi?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Education and social reform.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Savitribai Phule (3 January 1831 – 10 March 1897) is remembered for her outstanding contribution to education and social reform. She is regarded as India's first female teacher and a pioneer of women's education. (सावित्रीबाई फुले — शिक्षा एवं समाज सुधार)

• Along with her husband Jyotirao (Jyotiba) Phule, she opened the first school for girls at Bhide Wada, Pune, in 1848.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Phules founded the Satyashodhak Samaj (1873) to fight caste discrimination and promote equality.

• Savitribai worked against child marriage and sati and for widow remarriage; she opened the Balhatya Pratibandhak Griha, a care centre for pregnant widows, and died while serving plague patients in 1897.

• She was also a poet — her collections include "Kavya Phule" and "Bavan Kashi Subodh Ratnakar" — but her defining contribution was in education and social reform.

NOTE

• Her birth anniversary, 3 January, is celebrated as Balika Din / Savitribai Phule Jayanti. Savitribai Phule Pune University (formerly the University of Pune) is named after her.

question: For which English novel was Ruskin Bond honoured with the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1992?
option_4: Our Trees Still Grow in Dehra
solution_text:
The correct answer is Our Trees Still Grow in Dehra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ruskin Bond received the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1992 (for English) for his book "Our Trees Still Grow in Dehra", a collection of semi-autobiographical short stories set in and around Dehradun. (रस्किन बॉन्ड — साहित्य अकादमी पुरस्कार, 1992)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Ruskin Bond (born 19 May 1934 at Kasauli) is one of India's best-loved English writers; he lives in Landour, Mussoorie.

• His first novel, "The Room on the Roof" (written at 17), won the John Llewellyn Rhys Prize (1957).

• Other famous works: The Blue Umbrella, The Night Train at Deoli, Rusty series, A Flight of Pigeons (filmed as *Junoon*), Time Stops at Shamli.

• He was awarded the Padma Shri (1999) and the Padma Bhushan (2014), and the Sahitya Akademi Bal Sahitya Puraskar (2012).

NOTE

• The Sahitya Akademi Award was instituted in 1954 and is given annually in 24 recognised languages. The Sahitya Akademi is India's National Academy of Letters, established in 1954 with its headquarters in New Delhi.

question: Who was the successor of Vima Kadphises in Kushana dynasty?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kanishka.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Kanishka I succeeded Vima Kadphises as the ruler of the Kushana dynasty. He was the greatest Kushana ruler and ascended the throne in 78 CE, the year from which the Saka era is counted. (कनिष्क — कुषाण वंश)

• His capital was Purushapura (Peshawar), with a second capital at Mathura.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Kujula Kadphises was the founder of the Kushana empire in India and the predecessor (father) of Vima Kadphises, not his successor.

• Menander (Milinda) was an Indo-Greek king converted to Buddhism by Nagasena; their dialogue is recorded in the Milinda Panha.

• Kharavela was the famous Chedi ruler of Kalinga, known from the Hathigumpha inscription.

NOTE

• Kanishka was a great patron of Mahayana Buddhism and convened the Fourth Buddhist Council at Kundalvana, Kashmir, presided over by Vasumitra with Ashvaghosha as deputy.

• His court had scholars such as Ashvaghosha (Buddhacharita), Nagarjuna, Vasumitra, Charaka (physician) and the engineer Agisala. The Gandhara and Mathura schools of art flourished under the Kushanas.

question: In which region of Bangladesh do the Chakma people predominantly live, among the country's various indigenous ethnic groups?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chittagong Hill Tracts.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Chakma are the largest indigenous ethnic group of Bangladesh and live predominantly in the Chittagong Hill Tracts (CHT), comprising the districts of Rangamati, Khagrachari and Bandarban. (चकमा — चटगाँव पहाड़ी क्षेत्र)

• They are mainly Theravada Buddhists and speak the Chakma language, an Indo-Aryan language.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Many Chakmas migrated to India in the 1960s after their lands were submerged by the Kaptai Dam on the Karnaphuli river; large numbers settled in Arunachal Pradesh, Mizoram, Tripura and Assam.

• The CHT Peace Accord was signed in 1997 between the Government of Bangladesh and the Parbatya Chattagram Jana Samhati Samiti (PCJSS).

NOTE

• Bangladesh was created in 1971; its capital is Dhaka and its currency is the Taka. It shares its longest international border with India (about 4,096 km), touching West Bengal, Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.

• The Sundarbans, shared by India and Bangladesh, is the world's largest mangrove forest and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

question: Which Ministry of India launched the Pradhan Mantri Rojgar Protsahan Yojana (PMRPY)?
option_4: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ministry of Labour & Employment.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Pradhan Mantri Rojgar Protsahan Yojana (PMRPY) was launched by the Ministry of Labour & Employment in August 2016. (प्रधानमंत्री रोजगार प्रोत्साहन योजना — श्रम एवं रोजगार मंत्रालय)

• Objective: to incentivise employers to create new jobs. Under the scheme, the Government of India paid the employer's full contribution of 12% (8.33% EPS + 3.67% EPF) for new employees for a period of three years.

• It was implemented through the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) and covered new employees earning up to ₹15,000 per month.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The scheme's terminal date for registration of beneficiaries was 31 March 2019; beneficiaries registered by then continued to get benefits for three years.

• Its successor scheme is the Aatmanirbhar Bharat Rojgar Yojana (ABRY), 2020, also run by the Ministry of Labour & Employment through the EPFO.

NOTE

• Other employment/skill schemes: MGNREGA and DDU-GKY (Ministry of Rural Development), Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) (Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship), PM SVANidhi (Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs).

question: Who received the National Nritya Shiromani award 2019 for promoting Kathak dance form across the world?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Anindita Neogy Anaam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Anindita Neogy Anaam, a distinguished Kathak dancer and choreographer, received the "National Nritya Shiromani Award 2019" for promoting the Kathak dance form across the world. (नृत्य शिरोमणि पुरस्कार 2019 — अनिंदिता नियोगी अनाम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Kathak is one of the eight classical dance forms of India, originating in North India (Uttar Pradesh). The word comes from "katha" (story) — the *kathakars* narrated stories through dance.

• Kathak is known for tatkar (footwork), chakkars (rapid spins), tora-tukra and abhinaya, and is performed to Hindustani music. Its three main gharanas are Lucknow, Jaipur and Banaras.

• Famous Kathak exponents: Birju Maharaj, Sitara Devi, Shovana Narayan, Kumudini Lakhia, Gopi Krishna, Damayanti Joshi.

NOTE

• Options given: Jatin Goswami is a well-known Sattriya dancer of Assam; Anita Sharma is also associated with Sattriya; Aparna Satheesan is a Bharatanatyam/Mohiniyattam dancer.

• The eight classical dances: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (UP), Kathakali and Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur) and Sattriya (Assam).

question: Which Indian dynasty is associated with the creation of highly skillful bronze sculptures?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chola.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Chola dynasty (9th–13th century CE) of Tamil Nadu is famous for its highly skilful bronze sculptures, made by the "lost-wax" (cire perdue / madhuchchhishta vidhana) casting technique. (चोल कांस्य मूर्तियाँ)

• The most celebrated Chola bronze is the Nataraja — Lord Shiva performing the cosmic dance (Ananda Tandava) within a ring of fire.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Chola temple architecture belongs to the Dravidian style. The Brihadeeswarar (Rajarajeswara) Temple at Thanjavur was built by Raja Raja Chola I (1010 CE), and the Gangaikonda Cholapuram temple by Rajendra Chola I — both are UNESCO World Heritage Sites under the "Great Living Chola Temples".

• Pallavas are known for rock-cut architecture at Mahabalipuram (Mamallapuram) — the Shore Temple, Rathas and Arjuna's Penance.

• Mauryan art is famous for its polished sandstone pillars and capitals, such as the Sarnath Lion Capital (India's national emblem).

NOTE

• Chola administration is noted for its highly developed local self-government through village assemblies (Ur, Sabha/Mahasabha and Nagaram), described in the Uttaramerur inscriptions of Parantaka I.

question: What is Gross Domestic Product (GDP) in the context of National Income Accounting?
option_1: The total exports of a country
option_2: The total savings of a nation
option_3: The total value of all goods and services produced within a country's borders in a specific period
option_4: The total income of a country's government
solution_text:
The correct answer is The total value of all goods and services produced within a country's borders in a specific period.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Gross Domestic Product (GDP) is the total market value of all final goods and services produced within the geographical boundaries of a country during a specific period (usually one financial year). (सकल घरेलू उत्पाद)

• GDP is based on the domestic territory concept — it counts production inside the country irrespective of whether the producer is a citizen or a foreigner.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• GNP = GDP + Net Factor Income from Abroad (NFIA).

• NNP = GNP – Depreciation; National Income (NNP at factor cost) = NNP at market price – Indirect Taxes + Subsidies.

• Nominal GDP is measured at current prices, while Real GDP is measured at constant (base-year) prices, removing the effect of inflation. GDP Deflator = (Nominal GDP / Real GDP) × 100.

• Three methods of measuring national income: Production (value-added) method, Income method and Expenditure method.

NOTE

• In India, national income estimates are prepared by the National Statistical Office (NSO) under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI). The current base year for national accounts is 2011-12.

• The concept of national income in India was first estimated by Dadabhai Naoroji in his book "Poverty and Un-British Rule in India"; the first scientific estimate was by the National Income Committee (1949) under P. C. Mahalanobis.
